title: Correct cross-project metering when subaccount hierarchy changes
creator: Rishi Patel
description: Intermittent misattribution of token usage to the old parent project when a subaccount is moved between projects/orgs. Customers report sudden billing spikes on the source project after manual reorganizations or automated syncs from SSO provisioning. Root cause appears tied to the order of events processed by the attribution service during hierarchy updates combined with eventual-consistent caches in the rate-limiter and billing aggregation pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: When a subaccount is reassigned, subsequent requests are billed to the new project within 30s under normal load
No retroactive usage migration from move event; historical tokens do not get reassigned after move unless explicit migration job runs
Rate-limiter counters reflect new project affinity within 60s and do not allow the old project to consume tokens billed to the new project
Automated integration tests cover case where move and concurrent request streams overlap (move first / request first / interleaved)
Metrics dashboard shows resolved 'cross_project_attribution_errors' falling to baseline after deployment
steps_to_reproduce: Create parent project A and child subaccount X under A
Start a high-rate request stream from a service using subaccount X keys (100 req/s) to generate quota usage
Trigger reassignment: move subaccount X from project A to project B via admin API
Observe billing attribution in the billing-aggregator dashboard and rate-limiter logs for 120s after move
Expected: new requests billed to B. Observed: sporadic tokens still attributed to A for up to several minutes in prod-like env
investigation_notes: Reproduced in staging with event replay when we inject artificial network latency between user-service and tenancy-service

Root cause: two-phase update race between tenancy service and attribution cache population. Move event published to tenancy-stream, but attribution service reads stale tenant mapping from local cache while billing-aggregator reads updated mapping from tenancy-db leading to split writes
Rate-limiter increments use an in-memory owner key computed at request time; cache TTL 60s means owner may mismatch for a window after move
Billing-aggregator has a reconciliation pass but only for daily rollups; not sufficient for immediate attribution corrections
Found edge case: if an API key is rotated immediately after move, the alias resolution path still resolves to previous project due to out-of-order token-index updates in core-keys-service
proposed_fix: 1) Make tenancy move event processing atomic by ensuring attribution cache invalidation occurs synchronously before move operation returns to admin API. 2) Reduce attribution cache TTL to 5s for move events and add an event-driven cache-warm path that eagerly fetches new mappings after move. 3) Update rate-limiter to consult authoritative tenant-mapping via a fast read-through path on cache-miss, and mark counters with a short-lived pending-tag so billing-aggregator can apply idempotent attribution corrections if downstream mapping changes within 60s. 4) Add a migration-safe reconciliation job that backfills attribution for requests flagged with pending-tag. 5) Fix ordering bug in core-keys-service: ensure token alias index is updated in the same transaction as tenancy binding changes.
rollout_plan: Patch tenancy-service to publish 'move:preflight' and 'move:commit' events and ensure admin API waits on commit acknowledgement (canary rollout to 10% hosts)
Deploy reduced TTL cache and read-through logic to attribution service behind feature flag (FF: attr-move-consistency)
Deploy rate-limiter tagging changes with FF and shadow-mode enabled to collect delta metrics for 48h
Run reconciliation job in dry-run to estimate corrections and customer impact window
Flip FF to active after 48h of monitoring and low anomaly rate, full rollout over 3 hours
Deploy core-keys-service transaction fix in the same release window to avoid mixed-state surprises
Post-deploy: run targeted audit for recent moves in past 24h and notify affected customers if any retroactive corrections required
testing_plan: Unit tests for cache invalidation and read-through path
Integration test: simulated move with concurrent 200 conn/sec request stream, assert no requests billed to old project after 30s
Chaos test: add 50-200ms latency between services during move, assert attribution stabilizes
Shadow rate-limiter run to compare counter diffs (shadow vs prod) for 48h
End-to-end billing integration test in staging: ensure daily aggregator reconciliation picks up pending-tags and corrects attribution as expected
